Done. Reflection summary:

What this exposed: a recurring OfficeQA question type (statutory-debt-limit ratio → geometric mean → FX conversion) that had failed 4 times but only existed as a loose verbal pointer in memory ("fx-and-geomean-debt-limit ref") with no actual skill file behind it.

Root cause of this run's miss (109523 vs gold 109625): off by exactly 0.093%, proportional — the textbook signature of rounding the geometric mean (or the individual ratios) mid-stream. Each ratio is ~0.997, so truncation compounds through the product and the final multiply. The method was right; the precision discipline was not.

Actions taken:
- Created a dedicated skill `officeqa-statutory-debt-limit-geomean-fx` (research category) with the full chain, table location, the GOLD-verified anchor (usd_product 306138.775 / 2.7926 = 109625), the 1964 GBP divisor (2.7926, not 2.7912), the "subject to limitation" total trap, and an explicit FULL-PRECISION rule: never round any ratio or the geomean — round only the final integer.
- Replaced the stale memory pointer with a compact entry that now references the real skill.

Not new/generalizable beyond this: the arithmetic itself. The one durable lesson is the precision rule, now captured in both the skill and the broader rounding-traps memory line.
